subject: URGENT: Live chat latency spike — mitigation steps and monitoring
message_1_subject: Live chat latency spike affecting customer sessions
message_1_body:
Hi Hannah,

We started seeing a noticeable latency increase on our live chat sessions around 08:55 PT this morning. Users report long pauses between messages (5–12s) and occasional dropped streaming chunks — both human chat and bot assistant flows are affected. This is impacting active sessions across our support pages.

Attached are a short screen capture and a sampling of traces from our client (latency_sample_traces.txt). We also uploaded server-side logs to the link we discussed earlier.

Can your team confirm whether this is on Redwood's side or something routing-related on our end? We can flip any client-side flags if you recommend a quick fallback.

Thanks — Claire
Claire Zhang
Product Lead, Firenet
claire@firenet.com
[Attachment: firenet_request_screenshots.png (png)]
message_2_subject: Re: Live chat latency spike affecting customer sessions
message_2_body:
Hi Claire — thanks for the quick heads-up and the traces. We're looking into this immediately and I’ve looped in our on-call infra lead. Initial ask: if you can temporarily switch the client to non-streaming (stream=false) for critical sessions, that will remove chunking latency while we triage; we realize that impacts UX but it’s the fastest path to a more consistent token latency.

Short-term mitigations we recommend you try now (these are reversible):
- Set stream=false in the SDK call to fall back to non-streamed completion (reduces chunk buffering).
- Limit max_tokens to 256 for live sessions while we stabilize.
- Add header x-redwood-priority: low_cost to avoid routing into overloaded high-batch pools (we’ll verify this mapping).

We will also run a route override from our side to move your traffic to a low-latency pool and check KV cache pressure on the edges. I’ll update within 30 minutes with the actions we’ve taken and any console toggles you should confirm.

On call: dev.patel is investigating queueing metrics; marissa is coordinating customer comms.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
[Attachment: latency_sample_traces.txt (text)]
message_3_subject: Re: Live chat latency spike — initial triage notes
message_3_body:
On Apr 4, 2027 at 09:28, hannah_schmitt wrote:
> Short-term mitigations we recommend you try now (these are reversible):
> - Set stream=false in the SDK call ...

Triage notes: we see elevated token-queue latency on edge shard us-west-2 (service metrics: token_wait_p99 spiked from ~5ms to ~220ms between 08:45–09:20). KV cache miss rate also increased ~3x which amplified batching pressure. No signs of network packet drops — this looks like internal batching+cache pressure interacting with a specific worker pool.

Immediate actions I applied from the console (10:00 PT):
1) Route override: redirected Firenet traffic to the low-latency reserved pool (ttl 2h).
2) Disabled continuous batching for your key (x-redwood-batching: manual).
3) Lowered default batch size via route override to 1 (x-redwood-batch-size: 1) for chat endpoints.
4) Activated fallback variant: redwood-small-quant for sessions where latency > 500ms (header override x-redwood-fallback-model).

These are live; we’re seeing immediate reduction in p95/p99 across the affected sessions in our staging slice. Please confirm if you notice improved behavior.

Next steps: capture full worker traces (logs_20270404.zip attached) and open a postmortem (RINF-7321). I’ll validate longer-term config to avoid repeated manual overrides (autoscaling rules + cache sizing).

— Dev Patel
Dev Patel, On-call Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai
[Attachment: logs_20270404.zip (log bundle)]
message_4_subject: Re: Live chat latency spike — short-term actions taken
message_4_body:
Hi Claire — quick summary of what we did and next steps.

What we did (Apr 4):
- Applied a route override to move Firenet traffic to a low-latency reserved pool (temporary, ttl=2h).
- Disabled continuous batching and reduced batch size to 1 for chat endpoints.
- Enabled fallback model redwood-small-quant when latency exceeded 500ms.
- On-call captured traces and logs; we attached them and opened RINF-7321 for full postmortem.

What you can do on your side (optional but helpful):
- If you need immediate stability over UX, set stream=false in the SDK for critical pages.
- Reduce max_tokens to 256 for interactive assist responses during the window.

Current status: metrics show p95 latency reduced from ~4.2s to ~0.9s in the affected slice after the overrides. We’ll keep the override active while the postmortem identifies durable mitigations and will propose a longer-term routing/scale change.

We’re scheduling a short postmortem readout tomorrow at 09:30 PT to review root cause and preventive actions; we’ll invite your SRE if you’d like to join. If this incident materially impacted SLAs, please let us know and we can discuss credits as appropriate once the full impact is assessed.

I’ll follow up with the postmortem link and action items. Sorry again for the disruption and thanks for the quick coordination.

— Hannah
